title: finding(changesets): two pending changesets publish the retire-vs-remove discriminator’s UN-AMENDED two-prong definition verbatim into the CHANGELOG, outside every instrument that guards it
body:
Dedup keywords: `retire-vs-remove discriminator` · un-amended two-prong definition · pending changeset · CHANGELOG verbatim · `5942-retire-mobile-component-config` · `7519-retire-mobile-residue-types` · objectui#7678

Surfaced by the isolated at-tier contract review of PR objectui#9926 (record comment `5734125317`), which named it as needing a carrier outside that card's file surface. ⭐ **Re-measured in this seat before filing, and the re-measurement changed the claim** — see "What the relay said vs what is there". Filed by the `domain:ui` execution seat (seat 3). ⛔ Unassigned, ungraded, ⛔ no `domain:*` applied — routing is the triage seat's.

## The defect

Two pending changesets state this package's retire-vs-remove discriminator **in its un-amended two-prong form**. Pending changeset bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a normative rule about to be taught to every upgrading reader in the spelling objectui#7678's amendment exists to deny.

Measured on objectui `origin/main` `02bc27b084f8cf295f9173899cea2b55743c9442` at 2026-09-18T18:06:46Z:

| file | the definition it publishes |
|---|---|
| `.changeset/5942-retire-mobile-component-config.md` | "a tombstone steers authors to a named live replacement key … or keeps loud a key the docs taught as working" |
| `.changeset/7519-retire-mobile-residue-types.md` | "a tombstone steers authors to a named live replacement key, or keeps loud a key the docs taught as working" |

Both declare `'@object-ui/types': minor` and `'@object-ui/mobile': minor`, so both ship.

⚠️ **Neither definition sentence carries the surviving-carrier precondition** — the clause objectui#7678 added, and the clause whose absence objectui#9684 was filed about.

## ⭐ What the relay said vs what is there — the correction this seat owes its own source

The review reported that both "state the rule in its un-amended two-prong form". That is **true of the definition sentence and only of it**. Re-measuring with a concept net rather than a literal-phrase probe (⛔ the literal probe scores **zero** on `5942`, which is exactly the blindness objectui#9684 is about — its own control fires 6 on `7519`):

- `5942` reasons **correctly** two sentences later, in its own words: "the whole interface goes, so there is no surviving object to hang a `never` key on".
- `7519` likewise: "Structurally there is also no silent-strip hazard for a tombstone to guard: whole interfaces go, nothing ever parsed them, and the mobile module has never had a `zod/` twin to host a `retirementTombstone()`."

⇒ ⛔ **Neither reaches a wrong conclusion, and neither retirement is in question.** The defect is narrower and still real: the **definition** a CHANGELOG reader is handed is the pre-amendment one, while the reasoning beside it silently assumes the amended one. A reader who learns the rule here learns it wrong and will apply it to a case where the two versions disagree.

## Why it is invisible to everything that guards this rule

- ⛔ Outside `packages/types/src` — so outside the population objectui#9684 measured and outside the new `tombstone-discriminator-agreement-9684` pin shipped by PR objectui#9926, whose scope is that directory.
- ⛔ Outside the `changeset-claim-re-read` gate's question, which judges **name resolution, never meaning** — it asks whether a pending body names a file you touched, ⛔ not whether a sentence in it is true.
- ⇒ Nothing in the tree can go red on this, and nothing did.

## Not measured

⛔ Whether any **other** pending changeset states the rule — only these two were named by the review and only these two were re-measured here; the pending set is four figures. ⛔ Whether any already-released CHANGELOG entry carries the same un-amended definition, which would be a published-and-shipped instance rather than a pending one. ⛔ What the right remedy is: correcting two prose bodies is precedented and frontmatter-untouched (`check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` records it as its own legitimate case), but whether the rule should be **stated** in changeset prose at all is the same question objectui#9930 puts to the maintainer for the source tree.

Refs: objectui#9684 (the card the class was measured on) · PR objectui#9926 (the delivery) · review record `5734125317` · objectui#9930 (the open decision on where this rule should be stated) · objectui#7678 (the amendment) · objectui#5941, objectui#7526 (the precedent changesets the rule is quoted from).
